items.stem: Which discovery sequence is most useful?

options.text: Agent architecture → promised ROI → optional customer evidence.
Outcomes → use cases → workflows → data → success metrics.
Pilot deployment → discover the problem later.
Connector count → logo selection → certificate.

items.stem: Which question best reveals current workflow evidence?

options.text: Which feature would make the deck more exciting?
Wouldn't AI make this perfect?
Walk me through the last time this happened, including systems, handoffs and time.
Can we assume every user has the same permissions?
Only the workshop attendance count.
Only the number of systems to connect.
Affected population, frequency, business consequence and evidence status.
The most senior person's favorite idea.

items.stem: A use case needs five systems and an unverified write action. What should happen?

options.text: Record technical, permission and action dependencies before rating effort low.
Omit security to keep the workshop moving.
Assume all writes are supported automatically.
Call it a quick win because the user request is one sentence.

items.stem: Where does a high-impact, high-effort use case belong on the standard matrix?

options.text: Nice-to-have.
Low-impact/high-effort deprioritize quadrant.
Strategic bet.
Quick win.

items.stem: What should accompany a final first-wave use case?

options.text: A fixed ROI copied from an unrelated customer.
Business/technical owners, metric plan, dependencies, uncertainties and next milestone.
A guarantee of full automation.
Only an attractive title.

items.stem: A rare compliance workflow has low reach but potentially high severity. How should it be assessed?

options.text: Discuss severity and controls explicitly instead of using seat count as the only impact measure.
Always discard it because few users are involved.
Ignore risk because only time savings count.
Assign a huge monetary saving without evidence.

items.stem: Should the source's eight-dimension score be an automatic universal feasibility gate?

options.text: No; complexity score direction and aggregation need SME review, and rationale remains essential.
No prioritization method can ever be useful.
Yes; source conflicts never need resolution.
Yes; a high complexity score proves easy implementation.
